name: United States federal law (CFR, U.S. Code, Federal Register, federal courts)
_doc: The base pack. Every other US pack is meant to be loaded ALONGSIDE this one, not instead of it, because almost every specialist citation eventually resolves to a title of the Code or the CFR.

shapes._what: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(6)(i)(D) — title + part is the address; the subsection tail rides along for display but is not part of the key, because a file holding part 214 holds every subsection of it.

file_match._what: Three or more section numbers of the form 214.x is what a real part looks like; one stray mention is a cross-reference in someone else's document.

shapes._what: 8 U.S.C. § 1255(k). Accepts U.S.C., USC, U. S. C.

file_match._what: Two bare occurrences AND at least one that is explicitly a section reference. Either test alone is noise: a four-digit number occurs everywhere, and a single section sign proves nothing about which section the file is.
GPO text carries [[Page NNNNN]] markers, which is how a pincite into a Federal Register preamble is recovered at all.

shapes._what: Party names. This is the address of a case; the reporter cite below is its shelf mark.
Reporter citations. Recognised so they show up next to a quotation as its neighbours, but NOT used as an address: a volume-and-page pair alone cannot tell you which downloaded PDF it is.
